report.headline: Projected to hold roughly NBA-average usage (20.0%) after a 25.0% role in the G League, with a wide interval and an unreliable efficiency read

projection.text: The model projects a 20.0% usage rate in the NBA, matching the league-average usage of 20.0%, with an 80% prediction interval of 14.7% to 25.3% — a span close to two standard deviations of the league's usage spread (5.3%).

risks.text: Usage is projected to drop from 25.0% in the G League to 20.0% in the NBA, and the 80% interval (14.7%–25.3%) spans nearly two standard deviations of NBA usage (5.3%), meaning the model can rank this player among peers but cannot pin down an individual outcome.
The true shooting projection of 52.3% (80% interval 46.5%–58.2%) is unreliable, since the model fails to outperform a simple league-average guess for this metric.
The estimate is built on only 45 historical GL->NBA transitions, a thin sample for this kind of move.
A 16.7% turnover rate in the source season is a data point of concern for ball-handling as competition and defensive pressure increase.

strengths.text: In the source season the subject carried a 25.0% usage rate, 1.10 standard deviations above the G League average, indicating a large offensive role.
Scoring efficiency was above the G League average, with a 57.4% true shooting percentage sitting 0.33 standard deviations high.
Playmaking output was notable, with a 23.4% assist rate and 4.993 assists per 75 possessions.
The usage projection of 20.0% lands exactly at the NBA average, suggesting the model does not expect the role to collapse despite the typical shrinkage captured by the 0.529 GL->NBA usage slope.

uncertainty.text: The true shooting projection of 52.3% should not be treated as informative: the model's mean absolute error (4.7%) is identical to that of simply guessing the league average, so it does not beat the trivial baseline for this metric.
